key_insight: A deep learning competing-risk model using only pre-treatment oncology data can accurately estimate 1-year cardiovascular event risk in women with early-stage breast cancer.
clinical_relevance: This could help identify higher-risk patients at the initial oncology visit and support earlier cardio-oncology referral before systemic therapy begins.
method: Registry-based cohort of 17,051 women with stage I-III breast cancer or DCIS in Stockholm-Gotland (2008-2019).
Used routinely available pre-treatment features: demographics, cancer characteristics, planned treatment, comorbidities, medications, and healthcare utilization.
Predicted 1-year major adverse cardiovascular events with a competing-risk deep learning model and assessed interpretability with Fine-Gray models.
evidence_signal: Performance was strong and stable across 3-fold cross-validation, with a median c-index of 0.84 for 1-year MACE prediction and 0.90 for the competing-risk outcome.
watch_item: The model was developed in one regional registry and needs external validation and workflow testing before routine clinical use.
paper_title: Deep Learning-Based Pretreatment Cardiovascular Risk Stratification in Women with Breast Cancer
